work_packages.name: Where water lies is worked out on the CPU alone: a sea, a lake in a hollow and a channel with a current each have a level, a depth and a flow at every point
work_packages.quality_bar: A description of water that a GPU, a game and a later river solver can all be held to: every answer follows from the bed and the declared bodies or from a closed form, as the reference queries of a shipped physics library do, and nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: From a bed height grid and declared bodies, `thrum-water-model` answers at any world point: the body of water there or none, its level, the bed, the depth and the current. A sea is level wherever the bed lies below it and beyond the bed's extent. A basin is the connected hollow round its seed below its level, and a second hollow beyond a ridge stays dry. A chart gives its own level and current where its level lies above the bed.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected answers closed forms worked out without the model: a cone-shaped hollow's shoreline radius at a level, a ridge between two hollows, a tilted chart? Would a model that floods every cell below the level, connected or not, fail it?

items.statement: Where declarations overlap, a chart is taken over a basin and a basin over the sea, and a basin's fill stops at a chart's footprint. Preparation refuses, by name: two bodies of one kind that overlap; a basin whose fill, anywhere in its stage's declared range, reaches the sea, another basin, the edge of the bed, or a chart other than across its end; and a chart with a cell on its footprint's edge whose neighbour is neither ground above the chart's level there nor a joined body's water at weight 1. Level, bed and current are continuous across the grid's cells.

Each body has a stage, inside a declared range, that is added to its level; a stage set outside the range is held at the range's end and counted. As a basin's stage rises its shoreline moves up the bed continuously, a neighbouring hollow floods only when the water reaches its sill, and lowering the stage drains it back to what it was.

Each body takes four gains, for the long waves and the three cascades, from its declared fetch and the wind through `thrum-sea-model`'s spectrum. The most exposed body's are 1; none exceeds 1; each falls as the fetch shortens; at 10 m/s the long-wave gain is under 0.05 for a fetch of 5 km and the shortest cascade's is over 0.9 at 200 m. A swell adds nothing to a basin's or a chart's own gains: with a swell running and no wind their long-wave gain is zero, and adding a swell to a wind never raises the energy their long waves carry.
items.ask: Are the expected gains worked out in the test from fetch-limited growth relations and band integrals of its own, and not from the function under test?

items.statement: At any point each wave layer is held, longest first, so that its significant height is at most 0.6 of the depth plus the swash depth there: untouched in deep water, a remainder at the still waterline, nothing where the ground stands a swash depth above the level, and continuous between. The swash depth is the profile's ratio times the significant height the point's row gives the field at its gains, before the limit, never more than the margin height and zero with no waves. It is one value over a body away from a join and follows the mix inside one. The power the limit takes from each layer is reported, and is zero where the limit does not bind.

The f64 surface model gives, for a point and a time, the water's height (the level and each wave layer at its gain), its slope, the surface's velocity (the current and the waves' together) and the time derivative of height, and says the point is dry whenever the surface there does not stand above the bed: on ground beyond the water, and in the swash between waves. On an open sea it equals `thrum-sea-model`'s evaluator, and on a basin whose gains are zero it is the level.

A conformance harness takes any provider of water answers and reports its largest difference from the model in height, slope, velocity, depth and current over a stated set of points and ticks, and every point where the two disagree on the body or on wet and dry. Given the model it reports nothing; given the model with one basin's level moved by a centimetre, it reports that centimetre and the points the shoreline crossed.

A bed grid built from triangles holds in each cell the highest ground over the cell's centre. Built from a tilted plane and from a bowl, it matches their closed forms to within the height the ground spans across one cell.
`thrum-water-model` builds and its tests run with no graphics device and no dependency on `thrum-render` or `wgpu`, and it holds no preset, island, hull or water table.

A chart meets the bodies it joins with no step. At every point on a source end's or a mouth's edge the chart's mixed row equals the joined body's row, in level, current and every gain, and so does what follows from the row: the swash depth, the wave support and the surface's height after the depth limit. That holds under a swell and a wind, with the source's stage and the mouth's each at both ends of its range, at an end too deep for the limit to bind and at one 0.25 m deep. Wherever the receiving body's level plus the design's reach, 0.175 of the margin height, stands at or above the chart's own level, the chart's row is that body's, and the weight toward it falls smoothly to nothing over the 0.25 m above. Inside the footprint, away from the ends, the row is the chart's own.
items.ask: Read the test. work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, a swell turns to face a beach, closes up, rises and breaks where the depth says, and an island calms its lee
work_packages.quality_bar: Wave theory a coastal engineer would sign: every figure follows from the bed, the dispersion relation and a published breaking rule, held to closed forms on a plane beach as the nearshore models SWAN and XBeach are, and nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: For a still body over a bed, preparation gives each of the wave lattice's eight directions a lag at wavelengths a factor of two apart from 20 m to 640 m and at stages 0.5 m apart across the body's declared range. For water that reaches the bed's edge the lag is zero on that edge and beyond it. On a plane beach of 1 in 10 on 2 m cells, an 80 m wave's phase at 0°, 30° and 60° of incidence is within 0.5 rad of Snell's closed form, where the design measured 0.34, and its crests in 2 m of water lie within 1° of Snell's angle.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the expected phase the integral of Snell's law, worked out in the test without the model's solver? Would a wave that keeps its deep-water phase fail it, and one given the local depth's wavenumber at each point with no integral along its path?

items.statement: A component whose wavelength lies between two of those, at a stage between two samples, takes both blends at once. On plane beaches of 1 in 10 and 1 in 30 on 2 m cells, for wavelengths from 20 m to 640 m and every stage in a 2 m range, the gradient of the blended phase is within 7% of the gradient of a lag solved for that wavelength and that stage themselves in a metre of water or more, where the design measured 5.0%, and within 13% between the 0.5 m floor and a metre, where it measured 8.0%. A component given its nearest wavelength and stage with no blend fails the same assertion. Moving the stage through a sample leaves no step in the phase.
items.ask: Read the test. Does it vary the wavelength and the stage together, between the samples of both, and include a wave of about 113 m in a metre of water halfway between two stages? Is the comparison lag solved in the test's run for the component's own wavelength and stage, on the same grid, so that only the blend's error is left, with WP12.1 holding the solve itself to Snell?

items.statement: Ground above the shore margin is closed to the lag, so round an island a wave reaches every shore from the sea: wherever a component's exposure is above zero and the water is under 4 m deep, its direction of travel lies within 75° of the shore's inward normal, where the design measured 60° at most and the untransformed wave runs out of the land on the lee side. A component's exposure is the share of its 45° sector with open water behind it, 1 on the windward shore and 0 in the lee, its energy is scaled by it, and far downwind of the island it returns toward 1.
items.ask: Does the test's island have a lee the deep-water wave leaves through, and are the expected exposures worked out in the test from the island's outline?

items.statement: A lake that land encloses takes its own waves. For a bowl the test makes inside ground that stands above its highest stage, whose bed falls to half a wavelength of depth within a fifth of its width, with a declared fetch that gives it a long-wave gain above zero: every wet cell has a finite lag at every direction, wavelength and stage; in water deeper than half a wavelength the wave's length is within 3% of the plain wave's and its direction within 15° of it, where the design measured 0.9% and 11°; in 2 m of water on the downwind shore, 30° and 60° round from where the wave meets it square on, the wave's direction of travel lies at least 10° closer to the shore's normal than the plain wave's, and on the shore the wave runs along it turns in toward the land; and the transformed long waves' energy at a point is the gain's times the share of the declared fetch that lies upwind, under a tenth at the upwind shore and whole where the open water upwind is as long as the declared fetch. With the bed's edge as the only source the same bowl has no finite lag anywhere, which the test shows.
items.ask: Read the test. Is no wet cell of its basin joined to the bed's edge by water, and is the basin's long-wave gain above zero? Are the expected fetch shares worked out in the test from the basin's outline, and does the long-wave surface the model gives there have a height above zero at the downwind shore? A model and a test that agree on a flat lake prove nothing.

items.statement: A transformed component's height follows linear theory's shoaling coefficient at the point's depth, and the long layer is then held by the depth limit as WP1.5 holds it. A crest's breaking index is twice the envelope of the transformed long waves, before the limit, over 0.78 of the still depth. On a plane beach a regular wave of 1 m and 8 s reaches a breaking index of 1 in the depth linear shoaling gives, 1.64 m, at a height within 10% of Komar and Gaughan's 1.41 m, where the design measured 9% under. In a sea of two trains the highest crests of a set reach an index of 1 in deeper water than the lowest.
items.ask: Is the expected break depth worked out in the test from the dispersion relation and the group velocity, without the model?

items.statement: The breaker section is the profile's table over phase and breaking index, and the model refuses a table that breaks the design's rules: it adds nothing at index 0; its throw at each index is a function of the section's height that never falls as the height rises; past the bore index it has no throw and its crest and trough stand at the plain wave's heights. With the first profile's table the surface through a breaking crest overhangs near an index of 1 and never crosses itself. Inshore of the depth the waterline draws back to, the surface is the plain limited wave: WP1.13's beach gives the same waterline heights with surf in the profile.
items.ask: Does the test run WP1.13's plane beach with surf in the profile and hold the waterline's highest and lowest reach to the closed form? Does it search the thrown curve for a crossing at every index, and not only at 1?

items.statement: With surf in the profile the f64 surface model gives the height, slope, surface velocity and rate of height of the transformed and shaped surface, and says where a point is dry. Where a crest overhangs it gives the highest surface in the column, which WP12.12 holds. Without surf every answer is WP1's to the last bit. On a sea with no bed in reach the answers with and without surf are the same. The conformance harness reports a provider that leaves the transform out by the points where it differs.
items.ask: Read the test. Does it compare the answers without surf with WP1's bit for bit, and is the harness's provider the model with only the transform left out?

items.statement: The highest surface in a column is found by the design's cut of the sheet within the point's throw reach. On three sheets the test makes, at every point tried, the model's height lies between the least and the greatest height that the test's own cut gives within one cut cell of the point: a straight crest thrown as far as the first profile's table throws one; two trains crossing at a right angle, with heights of two to one, over a level bed shallow enough for their crests to be thrown; and a beach where three trains shoal and turn and the section follows the breaking index. The test's own cut evaluates the sheet forward on a lattice an eighth of the cut cell or finer, with no throw reach, search or inversion of the model's in it. On each sheet no thrown rest place the test evaluates is further from its own world place than the model's throw reach there, and every answer whose refinement converged maps to its point within the column tolerance. The plain iteration on horizontal displacement fails the same assertion under the straight crest's lip, and a scan of the throw along the crest's direction at the point, bounded by the envelope there, fails it on the crossing trains.
items.ask: Read the test. Is its reference the sheet's own forward evaluation on a finer lattice, cut by the vertical line over each point, with nothing of the model's search in it? On each sheet do the points include columns that hold three surfaces, and on the crossing trains a rest place set over its own world place, as in part X of `docs/evidence/WATERS/design-proof/surf_cut_proof.py`? work_packages.name: A float and a small craft ride the waves they sit on, at sea and on the lake, from rest to 15 m/s, and a float in a current is carried by it
work_packages.quality_bar: Boats and barrels as in the sea of Sea of Thieves: they lift as a crest arrives, tilt down its face, and never slide, jitter or lag the water. On the lake they sit as still as the water, and in a current they go with it.

items.statement: One dispatch per tick answers every posted point with height, slope, surface velocity and the time derivative of height, valid at the point's use tick, with that tick, the times its layers were made from and a support flag for each layer. For 2,048 points on a gale the long-wave part matches the model at the use tick within 2 mm, and the cascade part matches the model's cascades at the frame's time, carried to the use tick by their rate of change, within `SEA` WP2's bound, with each point's footprint choosing the cascade mip. Each answer also names the body of water at its point with the depth and the current there, as the CPU model gives them, and a point where the surface at the use tick does not stand above the bed says it is dry, on ground beyond the water and in the swash between waves.

At a 60 Hz tick and 120 Hz frames an answer reaches the game one to two ticks after it was asked for, through discarded frames and a stalled readback. An answer used at another tick than its use tick is moved once, by its time derivative, and counted. An answer older than the declared maximum is unavailable and counted, and the blocking-read counter stays at zero.

It is fine and sharp in the shallows and wider and softer in deeper water, it travels with the waves, there is none in a glassy calm, at night or under a cloud's shade, and none inside the hull's shadow. It never repeats, never swims with the camera, and has no edge where the window ends.

items.statement: Looking up toward the Sun from under water, beams of light stand in the water round its direction and sweep as the waves pass. They lean with the Sun and stay steep when it is low, the water beneath the hull is dark between them, and away from the Sun's direction and in a calm the water's light is even, with no banding or grain in a still.

work_packages.name: A pitching crest seen close is drawn whole, with no tabs, strands, bands or flashing patch on its face, on the Mac and in Chrome
work_packages.quality_bar: The breakers on the beaches of Horizon Forbidden West, seen from the sand and from just above: the white of a pitching face follows the curl of the water and breaks up as foam does, the underside of the lip is one edge, a front's ends taper into the swell, and nothing straight-sided shows or flashes in the face as the crest passes. The pitch, peel and connected bore are the ones WP13 passed. The reference shows what a cue should look like, and the lists in the items decide.

items.statement: On Metal, each cue that shows on the pitching face has its causes named from the submitted frame before anything is changed to remove it. The cues are five, each looked for in the views where WP20.2 judges it. (a) A gray straight-sided patch or a dark slit in the folding face at the upper-right bend of the exposed beach, from WP13.5's 40 m camera in a trade wind as three crests pass the bend; its known witness is engine time 5.22 s to 5.32 s at native x = 2200–2260, y = 345–370 at 2560×1440. (b) Bright straight-sided tabs under the lip, from 2 m on the sand looking along the break in a trade wind. (c) White strands with dark gaps between them under the lip, from 2 m looking out to sea in a gale. (d) A blunt or square white cap at an end of a pitching front, at the handoff view in a trade wind and in a gale. (e) Upright bands across the white face, in both 2 m views. The record holds a `realtime` take of each of those five views at the revision the work package starts from, and says of each cue, in each view where it is looked for, whether it shows. A cue that first shows at a later revision, in a view where it is looked for, is added to the record with the take that shows it. Each cue shown has a diagnosis for each view that shows it, taken at a revision that shows it and before any change made to remove it: one submitted frame at a fixed engine time, with the foam run from the scene's start, that shows the cue as the motion does, drawn three ways from the same submission (as shipped, with the foam left out, and as a reading of the mesh that marks which side of each triangle faces the camera), with a reading at the cue's pixels of the submitted depth against the model's nearest surface. The diagnosis names every cause its frames support, one or several of four: the submitted geometry, the surface that wins depth, the foam's cover on the face, and the water's shading. A view that shows no cue owes its take and no frame.
items.inspect: From the record, at native size: the starting take of each of the five views, any later take the record adds, and for each cue shown its three frames and its depth reading. 1. Each cue is recorded as shown or absent in each view where it is looked for, and the takes agree. 2. For each cue shown, in each view that shows it, the frame drawn as shipped shows it at the pixels the record names. 3. Each cause a diagnosis names has its observation in that diagnosis's frames: the geometry, where the cue stays with the foam left out on stretched or back-facing triangles; the depth, where the submitted depth at the cue's pixels is not the model's nearest surface; the foam, where the cue goes with the foam left out; the shading, where the cue stays with the foam left out on front-facing triangles at the nearest depth. 4. No diagnosis leaves out a cause whose observation its frames show: where two hold at the same pixels, as when the cue goes with the foam left out and the depth there is not the nearest surface's, both are named.
items.ask: Was each diagnosis taken at a revision before any change this work package made to remove its cue, and do its three frames share one camera, engine time and foam state, differing only in what the surface's fragment stage writes?

items.statement: On Metal a pitching crest is drawn whole from the sand and from above, in a trade wind and a gale. None of WP20.1's five cues shows in a view where it is looked for: no gray patch or dark slit in the folding face at the bend, no tabs or strands under the lip, no blunt or square cap at a front's end, no upright bands across the white face. The white of the face travels with the water over the lip. Each crest still pitches, peels along its length and lowers into a connected bore, and the throw is not taken out where the mesh resolves the fold. Each repair changes a stage that a diagnosis in WP20.1's or WP20.4's record names as a cause of the cue it removes. A repair that changes which surface wins depth is held on the target where it changes the winner: on Metal, at a cue whose diagnosis in WP20.1's record names depth as a cause, by a case in `surf_frame_gpu` that fails without the repair; in Chrome, at a cue whose diagnosis in WP20.4's record names depth as a cause, by WP20.3's depth reading. A repair that changes the winner only in Chrome owes no Metal case. The frame contract of WP13.9 still holds.
items.inspect: Use `realtime` motion and `fixed` stills of the repaired build: in a trade wind from WP13.5's 40 m camera, long enough for three crests to pass the upper-right bend, with a still at the witness's engine time; from 2 m on the sand looking along the break in a trade wind and out to sea in a gale, through the pitch of three crests each; and at the handoff view in a trade wind and a gale. 1. At the bend, in the still and as each of the three crests passes, the face and lip run on from their neighbours, with no gray straight-sided patch and no dark slit. 2. From 2 m along the break the underside of the lip is one edge through the pitch: no straight-sided tab, fin or blade hangs from it. 3. From 2 m looking out to sea in a gale the white under the lip is whole or breaks up as foam does, with no row of strands parted by dark gaps and no sharp-edged dark opening. 4. At the handoff view both ends of a pitching front taper into the water, with no straight blade and no blunt or square-ended white patch. 5. From 2 m the white of the face is not crossed by upright bands that hold their place along the crest: its streaks and gaps travel with the water down the face. 6. In every view each crest still pitches forward, peels along its length and lowers into a connected bore, with no row of teeth along the lip.
items.ask: Does each repair made in this work package change a stage that a diagnosis in WP20.1's or WP20.4's record names as a cause of its cue? work_packages.name: A visitor takes the water from glassy calm to gale, raises and lowers the lake, and goes from dawn to night with the controls, and it holds up in motion, on the Mac and in Chrome
work_packages.quality_bar: The whole range of the sea of Sea of Thieves: a mirror calm, a working breeze and a gale under any hour's sky, from the deck and from the masthead, with a vista to the horizon, stable under temporal reconstruction as a shipped game's water is. The lake and the channel hold across the same range.

items.statement: Wind speed and direction, swell height, period and direction, the tide and the lake's level, time of day and a field overlay are typed controls with the same keys, labels, units and ranges on the Mac panel and the Chrome page. A parameter file applies them, and five presets from glassy calm to gale apply on both with nothing refused.
In Chrome the page declares the same controls, and each preset and a parameter file apply.

At each of the five presets, from 1 m, 10 m and 40 m above the water, at noon, low Sun and twilight, the sea reads as that sea: flat and reflective in a calm, wind waves over swell in a trade wind, steep and breaking in a gale, with crests that sharpen as the wind rises.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills on the Mac's portable recipe for each preset, height and hour: the near water and the horizon.

items.statement: At each of the five presets at noon and low Sun the lake reads as a lake in that wind: a mirror in a calm, ruffled in a breeze, short steep waves in a gale and never the sea's swell. Raising and lowering it with the control moves its shore smoothly, and with the tide control moved too, no step opens where the channel leaves the lake or meets the sea.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the lake for each preset and hour from 2 m and 40 m, and `realtime` sequences of the level and tide controls moved through their ranges, at the lake's shore and at each end of the channel.

items.statement: From 40 m above, a vista of 1 km to 20 km holds: no tile or repeat, a clean horizon, whitecaps and haze that thin with distance, and no line where a level of detail ends.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills from 40 m in a trade wind and a gale at noon and low Sun, and a `realtime` slow pan: the sea at about 1, 5 and 20 km.

items.statement: As the wind slider moves from calm to gale over 30 seconds in motion, the sea builds with no pop, step or restart, and whitecaps appear as the wind passes a fresh breeze.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence of the whole change from 10 m above.

items.statement: Under TAAU on the Mac's portable recipe the water is stable in motion: no shimmer in the distance, no ghost behind the craft or its foam, no smear on the glitter, no crawl along a waterline or in the channel's carried detail. A camera cut and a rebuild of the water each reset in one frame.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences with temporal sampling selected, of a pan across a gale at low Sun, the craft passing at 12 m/s, a walk along the lake's shore and the channel, a cut, and a profile change: the far sea, the craft's edge, the glitter and the waterlines.

items.inspect: The same `realtime` sequences and the noon stills in Chrome, judged by WP10.7's, WP10.14's and WP10.3's lists.

work_packages.name: Still water mirrors the hills, trees and far shore that the camera cannot see, on the Mac and in Chrome
work_packages.quality_bar: The lakes of Red Dead Redemption 2 at dawn: the far shore, the ridge and each tree whole in the water whatever the camera does, joined to its foot at the waterline, softening and stretching as a breeze rises, and never cut off at the edge of the screen.

items.statement: On flat water the mirror lookup is a projection, and exact. For a bank, a post and a hill behind flat water, seen from 2 m and 10 m with the view's jitter on, each reflected ray reads the texel of the mirror that the scenery point its ray meets projects to, to a texel.
items.ask: Is the expected texel worked out on the CPU by projecting the scenery point through the view's own matrix, and would a lookup that flipped the image or left out the jitter fail?

items.statement: A mirrored reflection carries the right light. A matte panel of known radiance standing above the frame, 20 m and 3 km from flat water, reflects with the stored colour the optics equation gives, the air between the panel and the water included, at exposure scales sixteen times apart.
items.ask: Is the expected colour worked out on the CPU from the two stretches of the reflected path, camera to water and water to panel, with the Sun off the line of sight? Would a reader that took the camera's air off the mirror image, or applied it to the image a second time, fail it at 3 km?

items.statement: On the calm lake at dawn and at noon, with the camera looking down so that the far shore, the ridge and the tree are above the frame, and panning so that they leave its side, their reflections stay whole and do not change. Each joins its foot at the waterline, and nothing fades, stretches or ends at the screen's edge.

While a reflection can still be made out it stays joined to its foot at the waterline, neither sliding off it nor doubling. Under the island in a trade wind the sea carries the island's blurred reflection.
